Curriculum › Year 1

Year 1: what your child practises

In Year 1, Sharpwise has 30 topics in maths and 20 topics in English. Each one is below in plain words, with ideas to try at home.

Year 1 topics follow the National Curriculum for England. This page is made from the game's own list of topics, so it changes when the game does.

Play Sharpwise

Maths in Year 1

30 topics, grouped by the part of the curriculum each one practises.

Number: number and place value

Count in 2s, 5s, 10s
Count in multiples
One More, One Less
One more/less, counting back, to 100
Number Words
Numbers to 20 in words
Order Up!
Order numbers to 20
More, Fewer, Equal
Equal to, more than, less than (fewer), most, least
Number Line
Number line

Try at home:

  • Count stairs, spoons or steps together, then count backwards, and stop to ask what comes next.
  • Put two heaps of socks or coins side by side and ask which has more, and by how many.
  • Chalk a number line on the path and hop along it, asking where a number sits between two others.

Number: addition and subtraction

Number Bonds
Bonds within 20
Bonds to 10
Bonds to 10
Bonds to 20
Bonds to 20
Adding to 20
Add within 20
Story Sums
One-step problems, objects and pictures
Subtracting
Subtract within 20
Missing Number
Missing number problems
Doubles
Doubles
Doubles and halves
Doubles and halves
Balance the Scales
Equals sign, missing number

Try at home:

  • Lay out 10 spoons and ask how many more make 10.
  • Add the prices of two snacks in your head, then take one away to check the answer.

Number: multiplication and division

Arrays
Arrays, grouping
Share & Group
Grouping, sharing

Try at home:

  • Set out egg boxes or muffin trays and count the rows and columns to find the lots of.
  • Share a bowl of grapes fairly between family members and ask how many each, and how many are left.

Number: fractions

Halves & Quarters
Half, quarter

Try at home:

  • Share a bowl of grapes fairly between family members and ask how many each, and how many are left.

Measurement

Coins
Coins & notes
O'clock & Half Past
Time
Time Words
Time words, hours/minutes/seconds
Long & Tall
Length & height
Heavy & Light
Mass/weight
Full & Empty
Capacity & volume
Days & Months
Time (days, weeks, months)
My Day
Sequence events (morning, afternoon, evening; yesterday, today, tomorrow; before, after)

Try at home:

  • Let your child pay with real coins at the shop and work out the change together.
  • Ask what the clock will say in half an hour, then check when the time comes.
  • Compare a cup, a jug and a bowl: which holds more? Use a ruler or shoe-lengths to measure the table.

Geometry: properties of shapes

2-D Shapes
2-D shapes
3-D Shapes
Name common 3-D shapes

Try at home:

  • Go on a shape hunt around the house for circles, boxes, cylinders and right angles.

Geometry: position and direction

Left, Right & Turns
Position (between, next to, first, last), direction, turns

Try at home:

  • Go on a shape hunt around the house for circles, boxes, cylinders and right angles.

English in Year 1

20 topics, grouped by the part of the curriculum each one practises.

Reading: word reading

Joined-up Words
Contractions (I'm, I'll, we'll)
Real or Alien?
Decode words containing taught GPCs, including some pseudo-words
Sound Hunt
Respond speedily to graphemes; phase 3 & 5 alternatives, split digraphs

Try at home:

  • Choose three words a night: look, cover, write, check, and then say what makes each one tricky.
  • Say a word slowly, sound by sound, and ask your child to blend the sounds back into the word.

Reading: comprehension

Story Time
Listening; inference from what is said and done

Try at home:

  • After a bedtime story, ask who it was about, what happened and where, then how many or why.

Writing: transcription (spelling)

Sound Pairs
Digraphs
Tricky Words
Common exception words
Spelling Rules
ff, ll, ss, zz, ck; n before k; -tch; -ve
More Spelling Rules
ai/ay, oi/oy, -y endings, k before e/i/y, ph, wh
Plurals -s -es
Plurals
Join the Words
Compound words
Endings -ing -ed -er
Suffixes
Un- Words
The prefix un-
Alphabet Order
Name the letters of the alphabet in order
Days of the Week
Days
How Many Beats?
Division of words into syllables

Try at home:

  • Say a word slowly, sound by sound, and ask your child to blend the sounds back into the word.
  • Choose three words a night: look, cover, write, check, and then say what makes each one tricky.
  • Ask what the clock will say in half an hour, then check when the time comes.

Writing: transcription (handwriting)

Trace Letters
Handwriting
Trace Numbers
Form digits 0-9

Try at home:

  • Write big letters and numbers in flour, sand or with a finger on a steamy window.

Writing: composition

Story Sentences
Sequence words into sentences, and
Story Order
Sequence sentences to form short narratives

Try at home:

  • Read a few lines together every day and ask your child to point to the tricky words.

Writing: vocabulary, grammar and punctuation

Fix the Sentence
Capitals, . ? !

Try at home:

  • Look at a favourite book together and spot the full stops, question marks and describing words.
